clue.text: Football association secures revolutionary tie

indicators.note: a revolution turns something round, so the word it describes is read backwards

explanation.surface: A football governing body clinches a thrilling, game-changing match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Secures' looks like a container instruction wrapping 'tie'; it is really the verb NETS, and 'tie' is the definition sitting at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain verb synonym: tying a knot or a lace secures it in place.

clue.text: Joined around old college as directed

indicators.note: one piece goes around the other

explanation.surface: Someone joined up with an old college, as they were instructed to.
explanation.walkthrough: FUSED goes around O and C, giving F(OC)USED.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: attention aimed at one target has been concentrated there.

clue.text: Brown pea is pulped

indicators.note: pulping mashes something into a new shape

explanation.surface: A brown pea has been mashed to mush.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brown' reads as a colour describing the pea; it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Sepia is a reddish-brown colour, the tint of old photographs.

clue.text: Old dogs I directed towards Sally

parts.note: on = directed towards, as in 'turned on'

explanation.surface: Someone sends their old dogs off towards a woman called Sally.
explanation.walkthrough: Sally looks like a woman's name; with a lower-case sense, a sally is an outing or trip.
explanation.definitionFit: A less common sense of sally: besides a military sortie, it is a brief trip or outing.

clue.text: Dig dome out for Maui perhaps

indicators.note: out = not in its usual order

explanation.surface: An instruction to excavate a dome, perhaps on the Hawaiian island of Maui.
explanation.walkthrough: Maui looks like the Hawaiian island; it is also the demigod of Polynesian myth, and 'perhaps' flags him as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: Maui is a demigod in Polynesian mythology, famous for fishing up islands.

clue.text: Stand up unusual cleaning aid

indicators.note: the letters are in an unusual order

explanation.surface: A household gadget that stands upright, which is unusual for it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stand up' reads as an instruction or as describing the aid; it is only letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A dustpan is used with a brush to clean up.

clue.text: Masculine coat hung outside at first

parts.note: a mac is a raincoat (short for mackintosh)

indicators.note: take the first letter of each word it follows

explanation.surface: A man's coat has been hung up outside to begin with.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outside' looks like a container instruction; here it only supplies its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A near synonym: the word, from Spanish for 'male', describes showily manly behaviour.

clue.text: Dug soil up around LA to produce bloom

indicators.note: dug up soil is churned, so its letters are mixed
LA joins the mix of letters around it

parts.note: LA as printed, joins the fodder

explanation.surface: A gardener in Los Angeles turns over the soil to grow flowers.
explanation.walkthrough: LA reads as Los Angeles; it is just two more letters for the mix.
explanation.definitionFit: The gladiolus is a tall garden flower, so a bloom.

clue.text: Machine for deepening harbour deserted by river side

explanation.surface: A dredging machine sits idle, abandoned on the riverbank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deserted by' looks like a deletion instruction; 'deserted' is only D and 'by' puts the pieces side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: A dredge is a machine that scoops mud from the bottom to deepen a harbour.

clue.text: Setter taking test showing degree of optimism

indicators.note: one piece takes in the other

parts.note: the setter refers to themselves as ME, the outer piece
an oral is a spoken test

explanation.surface: The crossword setter sits an exam and reveals how hopeful they feel.
explanation.walkthrough: ME takes in ORAL: M(ORAL)E.
explanation.definitionFit: Morale is the level of confidence and optimism in a person or group.

clue.text: Big top a circus initially promises

parts.note: a cap is a top, as on a bottle

indicators.note: 'initially' means at the start, so only the start of 'circus' is used

parts.note: IOUs are written promises to pay

explanation.surface: A circus advertises its huge tent, the big top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Big top' is a circus tent, so the surface glues the two words together; they split, with 'Big' the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Capacious means roomy, able to hold a lot, so big.

clue.text: Box in clubs with speed

explanation.surface: A boxer fights, with fists or clubs, as fast as they can.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Box in' looks like an instruction to put something inside; 'Box' is the definition and 'in' merely links.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym for a slatted wooden container used to ship goods.

clue.text: Knight accepting thanks for one in flight

indicators.note: the outer piece accepts, takes in, the other

parts.note: a knight is addressed as Sir, the outer piece

explanation.surface: A knight gratefully takes a thank-you from a passenger on a plane.
explanation.walkthrough: SIR accepts TA: S(TA)IR. 'Flight' suggests air travel; a flight is also a run of stairs.
explanation.definitionFit: A flight of stairs is made of single stairs, each one in the flight.

clue.text: Admiring programme with roaming

parts.note: an app is a computer program

explanation.surface: Someone likes a phone plan that includes roaming abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With' simply joins the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Approving means looking on something favourably, admiring it.

clue.text: Lessening recession

definitions.meaning: a noun: a falling-off in amount or strength
a noun: a downturn, or a moving back

explanation.surface: An economic report notes a shrinking economy.
explanation.walkthrough: Both words read as one phrase about the economy; each on its own means the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A decline is both a lessening and a falling back, a recession.

clue.text: Barrel maker and wastrel regularly work together

indicators.note: take letters at regular intervals, every second one

explanation.surface: A barrel maker and a lazy good-for-nothing team up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'And' just joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the word is built from Latin 'co-' (together) and 'operari' (to work).

clue.text: Lay net out tidily

indicators.note: laid out, spread into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A fisherman is told to spread the net out neatly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lay net out' reads as one instruction; 'out' is the anagram signal and 'tidily' the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain adverb synonym: done in an orderly, well-kept way.

clue.text: Correction of last word on private message by hospital department

parts.note: amen is the last word of a prayer
DM = direct message, sent privately on social media

explanation.surface: Someone corrects the final word of a private message sent by a hospital department.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On' and 'by' only place the pieces in order.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a change made to fix or improve a text, as to a law.

clue.text: Hard growth on head alien bug

parts.note: a horn grows from an animal's head

explanation.surface: An alien bug has a hard bump on its head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bug' is the definition in the loose everyday sense of insect.
explanation.definitionFit: A hornet is a large wasp, loosely a bug.

clue.text: Cheater upset rabbi?

indicators.note: upsetting knocks the letters out of order

explanation.surface: A rabbi is dismayed to discover a cheat.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that a rabbi is one example of a teacher; the word itself means 'my master' or teacher.
explanation.definitionFit: A rabbi is a Jewish teacher of religious law.

clue.text: Exercise before cat returns

indicators.note: the word goes back the way it came

explanation.surface: Someone does their workout before the cat comes back home.
explanation.walkthrough: A press-up is the British name for a push-up.
explanation.definitionFit: A press-up is a floor exercise pushing the body up with the arms.

clue.text: Piano with a canvas covering is conspicuous

parts.note: a tent is a canvas shelter

explanation.surface: A piano draped under a canvas sheet stands out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Covering' looks like a container instruction; here 'canvas covering' is just TENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Patent (as in 'patent nonsense') means obvious, plainly conspicuous.

clue.text: Melody to pinch revolting seed

indicators.note: revolting = turning over, so the letters run backwards

explanation.surface: A song about stealing a disgusting seed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolting' pretends to mean disgusting, but it turns the whole joined string over, not just the word next to it.
explanation.definitionFit: A botanical fact: the 'nut' is really the edible seed from a pine cone.

clue.text: French fish with heart removed is toxic

definitions.note: POISON is a noun; 'toxic' is an adjective, loosely matched as in 'poison gas'

indicators.note: the middle letter is taken out

parts.note: the middle S of POISSON goes

explanation.surface: A French chef guts a fish because its insides are poisonous.
explanation.walkthrough: POISSON has seven letters, so its heart is the fourth, an S.
explanation.definitionFit: Poison is a toxic substance, and used before a noun it means toxic.

clue.text: Six deliveries by doctor behind bank arrangement

parts.note: in cricket an over is six balls bowled
aft = behind, at the back of a ship

explanation.surface: A doctor takes delivery of six parcels and falls behind with the bank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deliveries' suggests the post; in cricket a delivery is a bowled ball, and six make an over.
explanation.definitionFit: An overdraft is an arrangement letting you borrow from the bank beyond your balance.

clue.text: Headed back to hot island somewhere in India

indicators.note: the word before it goes backwards

explanation.surface: A traveller heads back to a hot island somewhere in India.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To' just joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by place: the capital territory in the north of India qualifies as somewhere there.

clue.text: Clamour about V&A furniture item

indicators.note: one piece goes about the other

explanation.surface: A public outcry over a piece of furniture at the V&A.
explanation.walkthrough: The V&A is the Victoria and Albert Museum in London, strong on furniture; here it only gives VA. DIN goes about it: DI(VA)N.
explanation.definitionFit: A divan is a low couch or bed.

clue.text: View six tailless deer

indicators.note: the last letter is cut off

parts.note: STAG with its last letter gone

explanation.surface: A scene of six deer that have lost their tails.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tailless' reads as describing the animals; it trims the last letter of STAG.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, from Italian for 'sight', usually a long, framed outlook.

clue.text: Marshal leading section for will

indicators.note: a section of the words is the answer

explanation.surface: A marshal heads the part of a parade put on for a will.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across the gap between 'Marshal' and 'leading'.
explanation.definitionFit: Shall and will both form the future tense.

clue.text: Husband annoys working dependants

parts.note: on = working, as a switched-on machine

explanation.surface: A husband is irritated by the family members who live off him while he works.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Working' looks like it describes the dependants; it is ON.
explanation.definitionFit: Hangers-on are people who depend on another for support or favour.

clue.text: More attention-seeking wild reindeer losing head

indicators.note: wild letters run in no fixed order
the first letter is dropped

explanation.surface: A wild reindeer craves more attention after losing its head.
explanation.walkthrough: The R goes first, then the remaining seven letters are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone needier demands more attention and support.

clue.text: Narrow passage artist represented

indicators.note: re-presented, the letters shown again in a new order

explanation.surface: An artist has painted a narrow passageway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Represented' sounds like the artist's work; it tells you to rearrange ARTIST.
explanation.definitionFit: A strait is a narrow stretch of water between two seas.
